messages:
maria_sre: @here Heads-up: planned NAT gateway replacement + ephemeral-route test across us-west/us-east tomorrow 03/25 02:00-04:00 UTC. This is a controlled drain: we’ll shift egress through new NATs and exercise our route-failover logic with a small loadtest. Expect short, benign 5-15s spikes for a subset of connections.

sam_oncall: Thx Maria. Which pools are in-scope? Any tenants that need opt-out?

maria_sre: In-scope: edge-gpu-pools (pool-a, pool-b), control-plane egress for metrics and artifact uploads. No tenant opt-out — we’ll route by region tag and only cut 10% traffic to the new path initially.

alex_infra: Added runbook + checklist: <https://go/internal/runbooks/nat-replace-1769>. Steps include canary switch, kvcache-warmup check, and rollback plan. I pushed the canary playbook to the release channel.

jamie_prod: Are we adjusting SLOs? Need to tell customer-facing teams.

maria_sre: Yes — temporary SLO window: p99 latency SLO for hosted API (generation) will be relaxed to 750ms for the 2h window. Error rate SLO unchanged. We will annotate the metrics and revert immediately after. slo-ops-bot will create an automated annotation.

slo-ops-bot: (automated) SLO annotation created: nat-replace-1769123456 window 1769123456-176912... details: temp p99=750ms.

sam_oncall: I’ll be oncall for the window. Paging policy: pager only for >1% 5m error spike or sustained 5m p99 >900ms. Otherwise post alerts to #eng-sre for review.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: nat-replace/ephemeral-route-v1 -> canary @ 02:00 UTC, ramp to 10% over 10min, 60min soak then 100% if green. CI checks passed.

alex_infra: Quick checklist snippet for the canary switch (paste for ops runbook):
```
# canary cutover
kubectl -n infra patch svc nat-egress --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/canary","value":"true"}]'
sleep 30
curl -sS https://edge-checker.internal/health | jq .nat_path
```
Verify KV cache hit-ratio > 90% on canary nodes before ramp.

jamie_prod: I’ll notify CS and Solutions about the temporary p99 change and the planned time window. Please add the message to the weekly ops digest too.

maria_sre: Post-deploy checks: verify per-route latency histogram, KV cache warmup, and artifact upload success rate. Run the following quick query in grafana: `sum(rate(requests[5m])) by (route)`, and check that any route with >10% failure is rolled back.

sam_oncall: If we see >2% 5m errors, immediate rollback. Who owns rollback? alex_infra + oncall.

alex_infra: Affirmed. Rollback is a single-step play: revert patch and revert gateway config. Script in runbook: `./rollback_nat.sh --id nat-replace-1769`.

maria_sre: One more: we’ll run a small synthetic loadtest at T+30m after canary (500 concurrent lightweight generation requests per region) to exercise cold KV misses and route switching. Expected token throughput ~ 50k tokens/min.

sam_oncall: I’ll coordinate the loadtest execution and watch the dashboards. I’ll drop quick logs here during the run.

ceo_alex: Appreciate the heads-up — please tag any cross-team customer impact in #incidents if visible to customers.

maria_sre: Copy. Will post a brief incident-like note only if customers observe degraded responses; otherwise this will be an internal maintenance broadcast. :thumbsup:

alex_infra: Final note: confirm firmware and kernel patch windows do not overlap in those AZs for the same timeframe. I checked and they don’t.

maria_sre: Thanks all — final reminder will go out @ 24h and @1h. If anyone needs to opt a particular internal integration out (e.g., large bulk artifact uploads), DM me.

sam_oncall: Understood. I’ll be monitoring and will post a short postmortem if anything notable happens.

maria_sre: Closing the loop: maintenance executed as planned. Postmortem posted in #postmortems (link will be here after review). :white_check_mark:
